title: RNA G-quadruplex structure recognition by chimeric peptides.
data_url: https://academic.oup.com/nar (supplementary material of the article only; no repository deposit)

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Read the full open-access text (82 KB) from the cached Europe PMC record, including the data availability statement and methods; counted every dissociation constant (Kd, the concentration at which half the target is bound) quoted in the text (10 distinct values) and every peptide name (6 variants: Pep11, Rhau18, Tandem Pep11, Cyclic Pep11, Rhau18-Pep11, Pep11-Rhau18); confirmed no sequence or structure accession anywhere in the text, no text-mined accessions, and no Zenodo/Dryad/GEO/SRA deposit linked to the DOI.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The contents of Supplementary Table S1 (oligonucleotide sequences) and Supplementary Table S2 (peptide binding data) are known only from the paper's prose: the Europe PMC supplementaryFiles endpoint timed out on two attempts, so no supplementary file was opened. Row counts for those tables are therefore inferred from the number of peptides and targets described, not read from a file.

a1_downloadable.note: Data availability says everything is 'in the supplementary material of this article'; the article is open access, so the supplement should be freely downloadable, but the Europe PMC supplementary endpoint timed out twice and I never opened a file. There is no repository deposit (no GEO, SRA, PDB, Zenodo or Dryad entry, and no accession anywhere in the text).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Binding affinity (Kd) is reported per peptide-target pair in Supplementary Table S2 according to the text, so the label would be a column rather than something to construct. Not verified in the file.

a3_inputs_present.note: Peptide sequences and RNA/DNA oligonucleotide sequences are listed in Supplementary Tables S1 and S2 per the methods, so inputs would be literal sequences, not accessions. Not verified in the file.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are explicit throughout the text: Kd in nM and micromolar (e.g. 99 +/- 6 nM, 2.82 +/- 0.97 micromolar), with standard deviations given.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL. The whole quantitative dataset is a handful of binding measurements: 10 distinct Kd values appear in the main text, generated by 6 peptide variants against a small target panel (hTERC rG4 wild type and one mutant, a few DNA G-quadruplexes and non-G4 RNAs). Even if Supplementary Table S2 holds every pairwise combination, that is a few tens of rows, far under the ~400 needed for classification and the ~1,500 for regression.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially small; the only large artefacts are molecular dynamics simulation trajectories, which were not deposited.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: No contradiction found, but also nothing to compare: there is no API record or download with a row count, only the paper's own prose.

a8_label_provenance.note: Labels are physical measurements - microscale thermophoresis and electrophoretic mobility shift assays done in this study - not another model's output and not computable from the sequence features. Provenance is clean; there is simply far too little of it.

existing_models.name: AGAPE (computational G-quadruplex Affinity Prediction)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved in detail; a bioRxiv preprint (2024) describing the first in silico workflow for predicting small-molecule ligand affinity to DNA and RNA G-quadruplexes.

existing_models.name: G4REP (deep learning predictor of human RNA G-quadruplex-binding proteins, Bioinformatics 2026)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported 86% accuracy separating RNA G4-binding proteins from non-binders, using ESM-2 (a protein language model) embeddings with an LSTM (long short-term memory network); split details not retrieved. A web server exists.

existing_models.name: rG4detector (convolutional neural network, Nucleic Acids Research 2022)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported to outperform earlier tools at predicting RNA G-quadruplex stability and detecting G4-forming sequences; evaluated on transcriptome-wide rG4-seq data. Exact numbers not retrieved.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (protein language model) for the peptide side, RNA-FM (RNA language model) for the rG4 side
backbone.hardware: Laptop CPU would be ample, but with ~10 labelled pairs any head is fitting noise.
backbone.licence: ESM-2 MIT, RNA-FM open; licence is not the obstacle.

integration.partner_dataset: G4LDB / G4-ligand affinity collections and rG4-seq transcriptome maps could in principle supply many more G-quadruplex binding measurements.
integration.join_key: RNA sequence or G-quadruplex motif identity; no standard identifier is present in this paper's tables.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Could not be written usefully: this paper contributes about ten measurements, so any combined dataset would be the partner resource with a rounding error added.

controls.positive_control: The paper itself contains one: the mutant hTERC construct must bind ~15-40x more weakly than wild type, and Rhau18 alone must bind rG4 better than non-G4 RNA. A model would have to recover that - but with 10 points this is an eyeball check, not a control.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling is meaningless at n=10.
controls.external_validation: None deposited; external affinity data for G4-binding peptides exists only scattered across individual papers.

honest_claim_h3: No honest model-based claim is available: with roughly ten dissociation constants from one laboratory, one assay and essentially one RNA target (hTERC), any fitted model would describe six designed peptides rather than predict anything.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use peptide and RNA sequence to predict how tightly a designed peptide grips a four-stranded RNA knot.
plain_idea.train_on: The project considered would show the model a peptide sequence plus an RNA or DNA sequence for each example. This paper supplies only about 10 measured pairs (6 peptide variants against a small target panel), which I counted in the text; the supplementary table was not opened.
plain_idea.predict: The output would be the dissociation constant Kd - the peptide concentration at which half the RNA is bound - measured here by microscale thermophoresis (watching how a fluorescent molecule moves in a temperature gradient) and gel shift assays.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Chemists designing ligands against RNA G-quadruplexes (knot-like four-stranded RNA folds involved in gene regulation and cancer) would use a reliable affinity predictor to skip synthesis rounds; but this dataset is far too small to build or test one.

more_or_better_data.why: This paper has roughly 10 affinity measurements. rG4detector and G4REP were trained on transcriptome-scale rG4-seq data and proteome-scale protein sets respectively; AGAPE was built on curated G4-ligand affinity collections. Ours is smaller by orders of magnitude.

confidence_score.why: Each Kd does carry a standard deviation from replicates, which is the right raw material for calibration, but with about 10 values there is no way to estimate per-prediction uncertainty that would generalise.

models_beatable.why: The nearby models are recent (rG4detector 2022, AGAPE 2024, G4REP 2026) and use modern backbones such as ESM-2; more importantly they solve different tasks (rG4 formation, protein binder identification) and none could be beaten using 10 peptide-RNA pairs.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails the first and third conditions: no existing model takes a peptide plus an rG4 sequence and returns a Kd, so there is no baseline to extend, and no joinable public resource measures the same quantity the same way at scale.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: predict peptide-rG4 dissociation constant from peptide sequence (ESM-2 embeddings) plus RNA sequence (RNA-FM embeddings), with the mutant hTERC construct as a built-in specificity control. Dead on sample size - about 10 measured pairs, 6 peptides, one dominant target.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, nothing timed: two small supplementary tables and a few dozen short sequences would embed in minutes on a laptop CPU. Compute was never the constraint.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the rows of Supplementary Table S2. The main text already answers it - 6 peptides, ~10 reported Kd values - which is the kill.

verdict_reason: Part A5 fails hard: this is a six-peptide medicinal-chemistry study with about 10 measured binding affinities, one dominant RNA target (hTERC) and one lab's assays. The measurements are clean, honest and physically grounded, but there is no dataset here - two orders of magnitude short of a trainable table, and no deposited sequencing, structural or simulation data to substitute.
